READABILITY.evidence: The module docstring and some comments help, but the parsing logic uses single-letter names throughout: `s, i, n, j, k, p, q, v, m` in `parse_tag`/`sanitize_once`, and `WS`, `nxt`, `a_s`, `a_e`. The branches of the long tokeniser in `sanitize_once` mostly have no comments.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: `sanitize_once` is about 95 lines with nested if/elif chains, and the comment, `!`/`?`, `</>`, script, drop-tag, raw-text and plaintext branches are all handled inline. The 'find `>` after `find_close`' logic is copy-pasted in two places. `rebuild_tag` returns a `changed` value that the caller never uses.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Files are read and written as latin-1 bytes, so the content round-trips unchanged. However, `sys.argv[1]` is not validated (no usage message or error) and there are no try/except blocks. It has magic constants (`range(50)`, `0x20`, `0x7f`) and silently cuts the rest of the file at an unterminated suspicious tag (`break`).

C6-01-CASE1.evidence: The rules are general: every `on*` attribute is dropped by lowercased name, and `parse_tag` handles slash/whitespace separators. `normalize()` decodes entities and strips control characters before checking `BAD_SCHEMES`, and only image `data:` URLs are allowed. `srcdoc` is sanitised recursively, `meta` refresh and SVG `values` attributes are checked, and object/embed/applet tags are dropped. Raw-text content is re-sanitised and passes repeat until nothing changes.

C6-01-CASE2.evidence: Edits are made on the source text, so quoting, attribute order and benign attributes are kept. But the cleaner over-removes: it strips markup-like text inside `<title>`/`<textarea>`, removes non-image `data:` URLs, and drops tails after unterminated tags. The hidden `test_clean_html_unchanged` failed, which shows it altered benign content.
